industry: Financial Services - Asset Management, Wealth & Retirement Technology
role_summary: Senior technology strategy and architecture leadership role for GWAM Asia, acting as Chief Architect responsible for aligning regional technology direction with global GWAM strategy and enterprise standards. Leads the Local Architecture Review Board (LARB), drives practical and responsible AI adoption, shapes shared technology service capabilities across Asia markets, and may oversee Asia operations technology. Requires deep architecture expertise across applications, data, integration, cloud and AI, combined with strong stakeholder influence across global, regional and market teams.
must_have_requirements: University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems or equivalent practical experience
Strong enterprise/solution/application architecture experience spanning data, integration, cloud, security and modern engineering practices
Demonstrated experience leading architecture governance forums (e.g. ARB/LARB) and making balanced business/risk/cost decisions
Proven track record applying AI in real business/technology contexts, including AI application delivery, agent deployment, or AI-enabled workflow transformation
Strong knowledge of SDLC in the AI era including AI-assisted engineering, model/agent lifecycle, responsible AI controls, testing and monitoring
Experience with shared technology services, reusable platforms and engineering standards across multiple markets or business lines
Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills with senior leaders, architects, engineers and risk partners
Strategic thinking ability connecting global strategy, regional priorities and local market execution into a technology roadmap
Experience in asset management, wealth, retirement or financial services technology environment
nice_to_have_requirements: Prior experience overseeing operations technology (production stability, resilience, service management)
Experience in a regional/APAC technology leadership role spanning multiple markets
Exposure to regulatory/compliance considerations in financial services technology
Experience coaching or developing architecture/technology talent
Familiarity with cloud-native and modern engineering practices (microservices, CI/CD, DevSecOps)
Experience with data governance and AI-ready data architecture initiatives

scoring_criteria.name: Enterprise/Solution Architecture Depth
scoring_criteria.why_it_matters: Core requirement to act as Chief Architect across applications, data, integration, cloud and security

scoring_criteria.name: Architecture Governance Leadership (LARB/ARB)
scoring_criteria.why_it_matters: Role explicitly leads LARB and must balance risk, cost, scalability in governance decisions

scoring_criteria.name: AI Adoption & Practical Application
scoring_criteria.why_it_matters: Central mandate to drive responsible, practical AI adoption and agent-based solutions
scoring_criteria.gap_expected: Candidates from traditional architecture backgrounds may lack hands-on AI delivery evidence

scoring_criteria.name: SDLC in AI Era / Responsible AI Controls
scoring_criteria.why_it_matters: Requires understanding of AI-assisted engineering, model/agent lifecycle, and production readiness controls

scoring_criteria.name: Shared Technology Services & Multi-Market Platforms
scoring_criteria.why_it_matters: Role drives reusable capabilities and consistency across Asia markets

scoring_criteria.name: Operations Technology Oversight
scoring_criteria.why_it_matters: Role may continue overseeing Asia operations technology stability and resilience

scoring_criteria.name: Senior Stakeholder Influence & Management
scoring_criteria.why_it_matters: Success depends on influencing global, regional and market leaders without direct authority

scoring_criteria.name: Strategic Thinking & Roadmap Ownership
scoring_criteria.why_it_matters: Must connect global strategy, regional priorities and market realities into actionable roadmap

scoring_criteria.name: Financial Services / GWAM Domain Relevance
scoring_criteria.why_it_matters: Domain-specific business context (asset management, wealth, retirement) improves credibility
scoring_criteria.gap_expected: Candidates from other industries may need to bridge domain gap via transferable architecture skills

scoring_criteria.name: Talent Coaching & AI Culture Building
scoring_criteria.why_it_matters: Role includes developing future-ready technology talent and AI-enabled ways of working

summary_focus: Position as senior architecture leader with regional/enterprise scope
Emphasize practical AI adoption and delivery, not just conceptual knowledge
Showcase multi-market or cross-functional stakeholder influence
Connect financial services or comparable regulated industry experience if available
do_not_overclaim: Do not claim direct GWAM/wealth-asset management experience if not present - use closest regulated industry equivalent
Do not overstate AI agent deployment experience if only exposure to AI tools/pilots exists - be specific about scope
Do not imply formal operations technology ownership if role was advisory/architecture-only
Avoid claiming direct LARB/ARB chairmanship if only participated as a member

cover_letter_guidance.tone: Executive, strategic, confident yet collaborative - reflecting a senior architecture leader who influences through expertise and relationships rather than authority
cover_letter_guidance.positioning: Position candidate as a bridge between enterprise architecture discipline and practical AI-driven transformation, capable of leading governance while enabling business-aligned innovation across a diverse regional footprint
bridge_gaps_honestly: If lacking direct GWAM/asset management experience, emphasize transferable architecture leadership in another regulated or complex multi-market industry
If AI delivery experience is emerging rather than extensive, frame as early adopter with hands-on pilots and a clear point of view on responsible AI governance
If operations technology oversight is limited, emphasize collaboration with operations teams and architectural contribution to resilience
